evidence.paper: The original paper summary reports that the authors analyze pre- and post-migration wages from the NIS and Migration Projects and that a pooled analysis shows larger wage gains for less educated workers, specifically that immigrants with no high school education gained more than college graduates. The paper describes wages adjusted to comparable U.S. dollar terms and compares wage gains at migration.

analysis_path.path_description: Run a median quantile regression of log wage gain on education groups, using college degree as the reference and estimating the no-high-school contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, age squared, and last home/U.S. job years.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Report starting row count.
Verify the required columns edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, country, lastHomeWageAdjusted, and lastUsWageAdjusted exist.
Drop rows missing required raw variables and report removals.
Drop rows with nonpositive lastHomeWageAdjusted or lastUsWageAdjusted and report removals.
Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs: no_high_school if edyrs <= 8, some_high_school if 9 <= edyrs < 12, high_school_some_college if 12 <= edyrs < 16, college_degree if edyrs >= 16.
Construct age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job^2.
Drop rows missing constructed model variables and report removals.
Fit q = 0.5 quantile regression with college_degree as the reference education group.
Report the no_high_school versus college_degree coefficient, p-value, confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, sample flow, final analytic N, and education group counts.

candidates.decision_summary: Task1 is high-quality. The original paper uses observational immigrant wage histories from the NIS and Migration Projects and studies wage gains from last home-country work to U.S. work; the focal claim is an individual-level education contrast in migration wage gains. The authorized dataset has 2854 individual rows, verified columns for education years, adjusted home and U.S. wages, country, sex, birth year, and job years, no missing values in required variables, positive adjusted wages, and extreme adjusted-wage maxima that support a robustness motivation for median regression. The code reads only data/wage_gain_table.xlsx, constructs log_wage_gain exactly as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), maps edyrs <= 8 to no_high_school and edyrs >= 16 to college_degree while retaining intermediate groups, constructs the planned age and timing controls, fits q=0.5 quantile regression with the declared formula, reports sample flow and focal output, and applies the fixed directional conclusion rule correctly. No low-quality rule is triggered: M1 and Task1 rules 1.1-1.4 do not apply because the estimand, sample, contrast, implementation, and executable code align with the declared path; M2-M6 do not apply because variables and restrictions are verified and justified. Guardrails G1, G8, and G14 were considered for the different model choice and absence of additional diagnostics; these are not defects because the median-regression deviation is explicit, evidence-based, and still answers the focal claim. The planning self-check had no unresolved failure.
